_comment: Run ids in results/experiments.db that must never appear in an analysis.
experiments/analyze.py reads this file by default and drops these rows.
The rows themselves are NEVER deleted -- a discarded run stays on record,
and the reason it was discarded is part of the record. Override with
--include-invalidated only to inspect what was thrown away.

excluded.reason: Three superseded E2 attempts plus a pilot and a two-trial link-down check. (a) ids 25-84 ran without continuous background traffic, so the network was under-loaded relative to the regime the model was trained in. (b) ids 89-122 were CPU-starved by wedged multipass clients on the host; because the arms run sequentially the starvation covered the entire B1 arm and none of P2, confounding host CPU with the system under test. (c) ids 24 and 85-88 are single exploratory trials, not a batch. The valid E2 batch is ids 123-182. See docs/limitations.md.

E2_B1_SHORTEST_PATH_packet_loss_seed3. Ran 21.5 min against a 5.1 min median: the post-fault iperf3 stalled for ~18 min with no timeout, so its 'after' sample was taken long after the fault had expired. It reads 3.02 Mbit/s against a 3.03 Mbit/s baseline -- a fully recovered network, which is not what that field is supposed to describe. Detection is unaffected (detected=False, no timings recorded), so dropping the trial does not change the detection rate for this cell; it removes a corrupted throughput value.

E2_P2_ML_RL_gradual_degradation_seed1. Ran 81.8 min against a 5.1 min median: the host slept and the guest clock was later stepped forward ~76 min to catch up. The incident timings look intact (detection 57.1s, recovery 65.1s -- not inflated by the step, so the step fell outside the detection window) and during_fault throughput is already an honest None. Excluded anyway because the trial cannot be shown to be clean, and the cell's detection rate is 4/4 either way, so no bias is introduced by dropping it.
